root_idea.summary: The root centers on stirring, releasing, or bringing something into directed motion.
root_idea.development: From excitation and removal of restraint, the lexicon develops into sending or commissioning, rousing and awakening, going forth, and divine raising of the dead.

senses.definition: To send, dispatch, or commission someone or something for a purpose or destination.
senses.usage_conditions: Used transitively of messengers, people, forces, witnesses, and other agents; the object may be sent alone or sent by means of another. It can also describe commissioning or bringing forth an agent for a task.

senses.definition: To send an affliction or punishment upon someone, causing it to befall them.
senses.usage_conditions: A construction with an affliction, trial, or punishment as the object and people as the recipients.

senses.definition: To rouse, awaken, or bring someone into motion or activity.
senses.usage_conditions: Includes awakening from sleep and bringing someone out of a resting or inactive state; it does not by itself imply resurrection from death.

senses.definition: To revive the dead and raise them to life; to resurrect.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of divine raising from death, including the raising of people for the Resurrection.

senses.definition: To go forth, set out, or become propelled into motion.
senses.usage_conditions: An intransitive Form VII use describing one who rises and proceeds or goes forth, as though impelled or sent onward.

senses.definition: The raising of the dead to life; resurrection.
senses.usage_conditions: A verbal noun used in the eschatological sense of the Resurrection and the raising of people from death.
The Quranic plural passive participle refers to people who will be raised for the Resurrection.

senses.definition: Going forth, proceeding, or setting out.
senses.usage_conditions: A verbal noun describing movement or departure, especially the proceeding of people toward a destination or task.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The removal of what restrains someone or something from free action.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A primary lexical notion of release into action or movement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Divine origination of beings, kinds, or species without prior existence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A theological classification of divine bringing-into-being, distinct from the Quranic usage of resurrection represented above.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To rouse, incite, urge, or put one another into action.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal Form VI construction, including mutual encouragement to undertake an affair.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To hasten or issue forth rapidly, as though propelled; of water, poetry, or other things, to pour or break forth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A broader intransitive Form VII extension describing rapid movement, flowing, or sudden emergence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become roused or awaken from sleep.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive Form VII use describing the subject's own becoming awake or active.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Sent; a person sent or a messenger.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verbal noun may be used as a passive-participle noun, including for a person dispatched on a mission.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A group or expedition sent from one place to another; an army or force dispatched in a direction.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A collective substantive, including a military force sent to the frontiers or to war.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Sleepless or wakeful, especially one repeatedly awakened by anxiety or grief.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjective describing a person whose concerns keep awakening him from sleep.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An occasion of raising, stirring up, exciting, or provoking sedition or a similar disturbance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun of occurrence referring to an episode or instance of such agitation.
The active-participle noun of Form I, used for an agent of sending.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An occasion, cause, or motive that brings about an action.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or causative use of the active participle, referring to what prompts or occasions something.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The Quickener of mankind after death.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A divine epithet referring to raising people to life on the day of resurrection.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A Christian festival associated with Easter and with prayers for rain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A loanword and technical religious-cultural term, not a productive Arabic derivative of the root.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place or time of sending; especially the time or mission of Muhammad's prophetic mission.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun of place or time that is also specialized for the beginning of the prophetic mission.
